A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEURONS study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains the earlier supplementary material and adds Appendices G and H.

before.justification: V1 reports original NEURONS reconstruction experiments, subject-specific results, component ablations, task evaluations and brain-mapping analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including reconstruction scores in Table 1, ablations in Table 2 and supplementary frame-based and concept-recognition results.

M1.justification: The brain model, four decoupled tasks, training objectives, progressive weighting strategy and aggregated inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix H summarizes existing components without introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain cc2017 reconstruction experiments with three subjects and the Algonauts 2023 data used for brain-mapping analysis. No dataset, population, task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: V2 adds MindAnimator to the video-based comparison in Table 1 using quoted results. The existing comparators remain, and the frame-based comparator set in supplementary Table a is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices C–F retain the same splits, preprocessing, training budgets, frame rates, evaluation metrics and analysis procedures. The added quoted comparator scores introduce no stated protocol revision.

E4.justification: The component ablations, qualitative examples, task analyses and brain-region mappings are unchanged. Removing the phrase 'failure case analysis' from Section 4.2 is editorial: the referenced Appendix E.2 and its examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The 100 repeated classification tests, existing plus/minus uncertainty reporting and preprocessing significance test are unchanged. The MindAnimator row follows the existing reporting convention without introducing new statistical procedures or run-count information.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds quoted MindAnimator results: 0.830 ± 0.03 for video 2-way accuracy and 0.428 ± 0.03 for CLIP-pcc, with no 50-way score. Existing numerical results and qualitative findings, including all NEURONS scores, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and formulations in Section 3 and Appendix B, including Equations 1–8 and the progressive weight schedule, are unchanged apart from punctuation. No assumptions, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reconstruction quality and visual-cortex alignment, including the 26.6% consistency and 19.1% semantic-accuracy improvements. The introduction rewrite preserves their meaning.

C2.justification: New Appendix G acknowledges limited dataset and subject diversity, low reconstruction resolution and frame rate, limitations of perceptual and narrative evaluation, and correlational rather than causal neurobiological interpretation. These qualify the retained findings without replacing the existing interpretations.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code and model weights from 'will be available' to 'are available' at the same repository, updating their reported release status. Implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing and hardware information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lu et al.'s 'Animate your thoughts' as reference 23, supporting the MindAnimator comparison. The related-work discussion and overall novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged; subsequent reference renumbering is incidental.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites part of the visual-cortex motivation, makes localized wording edits, and adds limitations and an AI-method overview for neuroscience readers as Appendices G–H. The main section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a comparator row and an updated source caption. Figure 7 is reduced in size, with local table and text reflow allowing the conclusion to finish before the references. Existing figure content, including animation frames, is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reporting completeness and qualification through the added MindAnimator comparison and Appendix G's explicit generalizability, evaluation and causality limitations. Appendix H also improves accessibility for neuroscience readers. These are useful, limited gains; the empirical coverage, method and central evidence remain unchanged.
